title: Measuring Scientific Capabilities of Language Models with a Systems Biology Dry Lab

content.abstract_summary: Introduction of SciGym, a standardized dry-lab simulation benchmark designed to evaluate autonomous LLM agents on scientific discovery tasks in systems biology. Systems are encoded as ODE networks using SBML. Agents must design experimental interventions (perturbations, dosing, sampling times) within a fixed experimental budget to recover unknown reaction kinetics and dynamical topologies.
key_findings: Establishes a standardized gym-like environment for evaluating LLM agents on nonlinear biological ODE systems
Identifies that frontier models without execution feedback struggle with stiff kinetics and high-dimensional parameter spaces
Provides reusable SBML-to-ODE simulation harnesses directly relevant for QSP and pharmacometric benchmarking
limitations: Focuses primarily on biochemical network topology rather than clinical pharmacometrics or population hierarchy (NLME)

extracted_claims.text: SciGym benchmarks LLM agent scientific reasoning through closed-loop interaction with dynamical systems modeled as ODEs in SBML.

gaps_addressed: Standardizes agentic benchmarking for biological ODE systems (feeds Activity 1 / QSP tasks and Activity 3)
